coordinate_system.orientation_notes: X is the longitudinal journal and collar machining axis. The mutually consistent front and right views establish Y as front-view height and Z as lug thickness and mounting-hole direction. Datum A supplies the planar reference, but a unique three-axis origin point is not specified. The front-view A-A marker describes viewing along +Y, whereas the section metadata states a Z cut normal; that inconsistency is not used to redefine the world axes. Uncertain isometric access directions are not treated as authoritative world-axis definitions.

The left slotted-hole position control references datum B, established by the right through-hole.
The right through-hole position control references datum A.
The collar right-face perpendicularity control references datum C on the cylindrical journal.
The collar right face is controlled perpendicular to the datum C journal axis.
The right lug outer-profile position control references datum C.
The right-view central width feature has a position control referencing datum C; its physical identity remains subject to clarification.
The lower flat face of the left lug references datum A on its upper flat face. Both surfaces are represented by the same lug feature node.
The left lug lower flat face is controlled parallel to its upper datum A face; this edge relates distinct surfaces within one feature node.
The annular collar and cylindrical journal share the longitudinal pin axis.
The right-view relief diameter and outer collar profile are centered on the same longitudinal axis.

The right cylindrical through-hole passes through the right mounting lug.
The left slotted through-hole opens through the surrounding front and rear contact areas.
The right through-hole opens through the surrounding front and rear contact areas.
Both mounting through-holes have axes normal to the lug faces along Z.
The four peripheral cutouts are described as symmetrically arranged around the outer collar.
The peripheral cutouts interrupt the outer collar profile.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: The left slotted-hole position control establishes A as primary and B as secondary. The right through-hole position control references A alone. Collar perpendicularity and the right-lug and right-view central-feature position controls reference C independently. No control establishes a unified A-B-C precedence. Datum A is carried by the left-lug node; its lower-face parallelism control references the distinct upper datum face within that node.

assumptions.text: right_view:F1 is grouped with the collar observations rather than the journal. Its description includes the projected flange envelope, and the reference image distinguishes that envelope from the smaller central journal.

section_aa:F2 is the provisional collar canonical because it provides the most section-specific axial and transition information. The differing front-view and section width callouts remain unresolved under C01; canonical selection is not authorization to machine either width.

front_view:F4 and isometric_view:F1 are grouped as whole-body observations. They are kept separate from the journal observations because overall component length and local journal length describe different scopes.
isometric_view:F2 and section_aa:F3 are grouped by the unique cylindrical segment between the collar and opposing lug transition. The dimensioned datum C section observation is canonical.

isometric_view:F4 is treated as an aggregate of two distinct lugs and contributes to separate left- and right-lug groups. Their different locations and datum/control identities prevent collapsing them into one interchangeable feature.

front_view:F7 and section_aa:F4 describe the same right lug. The front observation is canonical for its dimensioned outer profile; the section edge-break radius is retained as a separate callout scope rather than interpreted as a conflicting outer corner radius.

isometric_view:F5 is treated as an aggregate contributing to the two individually identified mounting holes. The left slotted hole and right datum B cylindrical hole remain separate physical features.
right_view:F4 remains a singleton pending C02. Shared datum C and position-control similarity are insufficient to merge a feature described as a slot or drive tang with the right lug.

front_view:F2 and front_view:F6 remain separate singleton feature families, each retaining its stated two-sided multiplicity. Neither pair is expanded into individually identified faces because no separate face observations are supplied.

The front and right views are used for world-axis orientation because their coordinate notes agree. The contradictory section cut-normal metadata and uncertain isometric transverse directions are not used to change that frame.

Datum A is represented by its containing left-lug feature rather than a new face node. The self-referencing datum and parallelism edges therefore connect the lower controlled face to the distinct upper datum face within that feature.

right_view:F2 and right_view:F3 remain separate relief and cutout features. Their absence from other feature lists or visibility limitations in the reference image is not grounds for merging or discarding them.
The four peripheral collar cutouts extend completely through the full thickness of the collar.
The hatched contact areas on the left lug are flush with the adjacent lug faces with zero recess depth.
The hatched contact areas on the right lug are flush with the adjacent lug faces with zero recess depth.

The Section A-A callout '2X 6.63 O/R' specifies the collar width measured over the outer radii at the tip, which tapers via the 2X 1.5° draft angle to the 7.63 collar width at the base. As an active Revision B1 callout, the 6.63 O/R dimension governs the outer collar thickness.

The 12.15/11.85 dimension specifies the projected thickness of the right mounting lug rather than a machined axial slot. It defines the distance between the two parallel outer faces of the lug as viewed along the axial direction.

The finished thickness of the left mounting lug along the Z-axis is not explicitly dimensioned on the 2D drawing and is defined by the master 3D CAD model per the drawing note '-CAD IS MASTER- FOR ANY DETAIL NOT SHOWN SEE CAD MODEL'. Its finished surfaces are geometrically controlled by Datum A with 0.2 mm flatness and 0.3 mm parallelism to Datum A (with 0.1 mm flatness on the Ø35.5/34.5 spotface areas).

The axial width of the right-view undercut relief (Ø70.00 U/R TYP.) is assumed to be 5.0 mm, corresponding to the 5.0 mm radial relief depth from the Ø80 nominal outer diameter and the 4X R5.0 corner radius.
